subject: Urban Planning
title: The Croton Aqueduct: New York Gets Clean Water
description: A quick win: understand The Croton Aqueduct: New York Gets Clean Water.

hook.text: In the 1830s, New Yorkers drank from wells contaminated by privies and graveyards. Cholera killed 3,500 in a single summer.

buildup.text: The city built the Croton Aqueduct — 41 miles of masonry channel bringing clean water from upstate reservoirs.

discovery.text: When the Croton arrived in 1842, crowds celebrated. Fountains erupted in City Hall Park. The water tasted like life.

twist.text: New York now controls 2,000 square miles of watershed upstate. Rural communities resent the city's control of their land.

climax.text: New York's water is so clean it doesn't require filtration — one of only five major US cities with unfiltered supply.

punchline.text: Protect the watershed. Skip the treatment plant. New York's been doing it since 1842.

quiz.question: Why doesn't New York City need to filter its tap water?
options: The city adds extra chlorine that makes filtration unnecessary
Its protected watershed keeps the source water naturally clean
Underground aquifers naturally purify the water before delivery
